probe: Determine whether an already-present Git object can be recovered by immutable object identity using lightweight repository transport, avoiding the external content-residency dependency that falsified the IPFS candidate.

observations: Git objects are immutable after creation and have object IDs derived from their type and contents.
The documented data model states that exact object contents can be recovered from an object ID as long as the object has not been deleted.
GitHub's Git database REST API exposes raw Git objects for repository reads and writes, including a Get a blob endpoint keyed by file_sha.
Get a blob is addressed by file_sha and can return raw blob data or base64 content.
The documented endpoint supports blobs up to 100 MB; public resources may be read without authentication, while private access requires ordinary repository Contents read permission.

Generic upload-pack fetching of unadvertised object IDs is capability-dependent; allow-tip-sha1-in-want and allow-reachable-sha1-in-want govern such wants, so arbitrary-OID native Git fetch is not treated as universally available.

GitHub REST transport is rate-limited; this is treated as a transient transport bound requiring cross-invocation resume, not as hosted compute and not as evidence of a monthly/trial/paid quota-free guarantee beyond the tested call.

direct_test.object_role: own prior cross_field r330 checkpoint blob
direct_test.transport: connected GitHub lightweight fetch_blob by exact object SHA

reasoning: Repository-native object identity removes the separate provider/pinning residency primitive required by the rejected IPFS path for content that is already present in the repository's Git object database.

The actual role-local test retrieved the prior r330 checkpoint blob by its exact object SHA through the connected GitHub transport, directly demonstrating object-ID-addressed recovery in this environment for one existing blob.

Git's immutable object model supplies an independent integrity relation between object identity and type/content, while GitHub documents a blob-by-SHA read surface. This combination is a stronger transversal transport/reconstruction primitive than external content-addressed residency for already-present repository objects.

The result does not prove indefinite retention of unreachable objects, retrieval beyond documented size limits, universal native Git-protocol arbitrary-OID fetch, operation during rate-limit exhaustion, SHA-256 repository support, or that future arbitrary payloads can be added without consuming hosted-storage capacity. Those remain unresolved children rather than accepted assumptions.
tested_scope: Public Git/GitHub object-model and Git-database documentation plus one live read-only retrieval of the existing own-role blob a20479c1bd3da5e4e24e1c4825785158cbad5089 from bachikoljunior-blip/note by exact object SHA. No object creation, repository-content mutation outside this authorized checkpoint chain, hosted compute, external storage, protected execution, manual user action, arbitrary unadvertised upload-pack request, rate-limit exhaustion test, >100MB blob test, unreachable-object retention test, or SHA-256 repository test.
scope_negative: No claim of permanent retention for unreachable Git objects, no claim that all Git servers allow arbitrary object-ID wants, no claim that GitHub REST is unlimited, no claim that adding new payload blobs is storage-quota-free, no claim for blobs above 100 MB, no claim for SHA-256 GitHub repositories, and no claim of whole-root richer-mode parity.
